recentItems.title: Huawei goes on trial in the US for racketeering
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies went on trial in the US on Tuesday on criminal charges after eight years of legal wrangling with the US government. The Shenzhen-based company has pleaded not guilty to all 14 counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, trade secret theft and racketeering, with the alleged criminal activity dating back to 1999.

recentItems.title: WATCH: Hong Kong’s first astronaut Lai Ka-ying gives live lecture from space
recentItems.description:
Hong Kong’s first astronaut Lai Ka-ying and her two fellow Shenzhou-23 crew members are delivering a live lecture from space. The activity, jointly organised by the Hong Kong and Macau governments and the China Manned Space Agency, includes an expert lecture, an in-orbit demonstration and a question-and-answer session to showcase the environment in space.

Source:
Information Services Department

recentItems.title: How Nepal tunnel flood survivors made it out alive
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more: https://sc.mp/no7d2

Rescuers continue to search for hundreds of hydropower workers believed trapped inside tunnels flooded during the August 26 glacial collapse disaster near the China-Nepal border. Two workers were rescued on Friday from the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower project and a Chinese national was found in another tunnel the following day. Rescuers and family members have recounted the harrowing days leading up to their dramatic rescue.

recentItems.title: Families pray for flood victims on day of mourning in Nepal
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Nepal observed a national day of mourning following a devastating glacial collapse near the China-Nepal border last month that unleashed deadly flash floods. At least 1,380 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,500 others remain missing. While some families have been reunited with survivors, others marked the day by continuing to hold out hope that their loved ones will be found alive.

recentItems.title: Meet the dogs trained to sniff out cancer with an AI boost
recentItems.description:
Sniffer dogs may soon be an easy, fast and affordable way to detect cancer, according to an Indian company that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to better interpret natural canine skills. Bengaluru-based start-up Dognosis boasts a 90 per cent accuracy rate for detecting seven major types of cancer, citing a study of 1,500 participants across six hospitals.

recentItems.title: North Korea launches second nuclear destroyer in 75 days
recentItems.description:
Read more: https://sc.mp/7ab2fa

North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has commissioned the country’s second naval destroyer, state media reported on Monday. The vessel equipped with nuclear-capable missiles was launched Sunday, the day before the US, South Korea and Japan started their latest trilateral military exercise, which Pyongyang sees as a security threat. North Korea has continued to dial up pressure on Washington after rebuffing US President Donald Trump’s conciliatory move to scale back US participation in a major military drill with South Korea last month.

recentItems.title: Many no-shows on first days of new booking system for scenic HK hiking trail
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hong Kong authorities will review a new reservation system for a Sai Kung trail famed for its dramatic volcanic rock columns after the National Day “golden week” in October, following large numbers of no-shows during the first two trial runs. Only 1,560 registered and walk-in patrons arrived at Po Pin Chau on Saturday and Sunday, despite 3,230 people having made bookings under the real-name reservation system. Lawmakers and a district councillor have called for more on-site quotas, clearer booking status information for walk-ins, and a penalty-points system to curb no-shows.

recentItems.title: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatoa covers cities in volcanic ash
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Indonesia’s Anak Krakatoa volcano erupted continuously for three days, beginning with an initial blast late Friday night. The nation’s meteorological agency reported two significant eruptions on Sunday that sent volcanic ash more than 150km (83 miles) away and across five provinces. Residents in the capital Jakarta were among those finding homes and cars covered in ashfall. Eight airports in the country were forced to suspend operations, stranding more than 170,000 passengers.

recentItems.title: International media allowed in China’s Gyirong Port
recentItems.description:
Chinese authorities announced on Sunday that search teams have retrieved 12 additional bodies, as efforts persist to locate hundreds who remain unaccounted for following the glacial collapse and subsequent massive flash flood that devastated China's primary border crossing with Nepal. Forty-three people have been confirmed dead and 519 remain missing on the Chinese side 11 days after the disaster. The announcement came as a small contingent of foreign media were allowed to visit the port for the first time since the deadly flash floods.
